title: Total Variation Denoising with Overlapping Group Sparsity
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing (ICASSP)

citations.claim: Selesnick and Chen extended total variation denoising by incorporating overlapping group sparsity, assuming that large values of the first-order difference function tend to cluster together rather than occur in isolation, thereby alleviating the staircase artifact inherent to standard TV denoising.

The group-sparse total variation (GS-TV) cost function is convex and uses a penalty that applies an L2 norm over sliding windows of size K on the difference signal, promoting structured sparsity in the derivative domain.

Selesnick and Chen derived an efficient iterative algorithm for GS-TV denoising using the majorization-minimization (MM) framework, where each iteration requires solving only a tridiagonal (banded) system of linear equations, making the algorithm computationally efficient and free of step-size parameters.

The MM algorithm for GS-TV denoising uses a quadratic majorizer of the group-sparsity penalty, leading to iteratively reweighted least squares updates where the diagonal weight matrix depends on local group norms of the current iterate.
Standard total variation denoising is a special case of GS-TV with group size K=1, where the penalty reduces to the L1 norm of the first-order difference.

Selesnick and Chen demonstrated that GS-TV denoising achieves lower RMSE than standard TV denoising on signals with smooth transitions, as the overlapping group penalty smooths the sparse derivative rather than producing isolated large values.
The MM algorithm avoids auxiliary variables and excess memory proportional to the group size, unlike previous algorithms for overlapping group sparsity that use variable splitting or replication.

do_not_claim: GS-TV was applied to chromatogram baseline correction
Selesnick and Chen used deep learning or neural networks in this work
GS-TV addresses the signal model y = x + f + n with separate baseline and peak components
This paper introduced the BEADS algorithm
